Routing notes (updated)

Confirmed valid:
- REQ-2407: large claim, south -> B (priority desk) accepted.
- REQ-2408: small shipment, north -> C (regional office) accepted.

Confirmed invalid:
- C rejected for: large claim south; large refund south; small claim north; large shipment east; small shipment east (plus earlier duplicates). C is not a safe default.
- B rejected for: large refund, east (REQ-2409).

Implications:
- Use B only when the case matches large claim + south unless more evidence supports wider use.
- Use C only when the case matches small shipment + north.
- A (standard queue) has not been tried in the logs; it is the likely fallback for unmatched cases, especially large refunds, small claims, east shipments, and any case where B/C are known invalid.
- Type, size, and region matter. Sender/department and subject phrases (“client asking twice”, “second attempt”, “scanned not typed”, “came through regional office”) did not predict success.

Open questions:
- Test A for large refunds, small claims north, and east shipments.
- Gather more data before generalizing B/C beyond the two confirmed pairs.
- Avoid defaulting to C; it was rejected in nearly every tested case.

Routing notes (updated)

Confirmed valid:
- REQ-2407 large claim, south -> B accepted.
- REQ-2408 small shipment, north -> C accepted.
- A accepted for: small claim east (2410); large claim east (2413, 2415); small claim south (2418); small shipment south (2419).

Confirmed invalid:
- C invalid: large claim south; large refund south; small claim north; large shipment east; small shipment east; earlier duplicates. C is not a safe default.
- B invalid: large refund east (2409).
- A invalid: large invoice north (2411); large invoice east (2414); large shipment north (2412); large shipment south (2416); small shipment east (2417).

Implications:
- Claims: B only for large claim + south. A works for east claims (large/small) and small claim south. Test A for small claim north; B/C unknown there.
- Shipments: C only for small shipment + north. A works for small shipment south. A and C fail for small shipment east; large shipments failed A (north/south) and C (east). Need tests for large shipments and east small shipments.
- Invoices/refunds: no confirmed valid route yet. A failed large invoices north/east. B failed large refund east; C failed large refund south. Test A for large refunds, and B/C for invoices/refunds.
- Sender/department and subject phrases still not predictive.

Open questions:
- Which option handles invoices, refunds, large shipments, small shipments east, small claims north?
- Use only confirmed pairs; avoid defaulting to A, B, or C for unmatched cases.
